symptoms: asks me to clean pogo pins every two days
cleaning reminder keeps coming back
toolhead cleaning notification every day
fixes.title: Pogo cleaning reminder keeps returning
fixes.likely_cause: The brief describes either a reminder-state problem or an unreliable contact; frequent alerts alone do not prove dirt is the cause.
steps: Stop the print and use the official contact-cleaning procedure with the machine in its specified safe state.
Inspect and photograph the contact surfaces; reseat the head only as directed in the maintenance guide.
Record which head triggers the reminder and send the pattern and photos to support if cleaning does not resolve it.
fixes.stop_if: A contact is bent, stuck, recessed or visibly damaged, or a fan also drops out. Stop using that head and contact support.

symptoms: homing moves the head the wrong way
homing anomaly move head to bed center
printer starts homing from the corner
fixes.title: Homing begins from an unexpected position
fixes.likely_cause: The brief reports a recovery involving the head's starting position. Mechanical obstruction or an unresolved setup fault can look similar.
steps: Cancel motion if the head approaches an obstruction; save the displayed message and starting position.
Check the official homing and setup instructions for the correct recovery sequence.
If the official guide or support directs you to center the head, do so only in the machine state they specify, then retry once.
fixes.stop_if: The nozzle scrapes the plate, motion binds, or a controlled retry fails. Contact support before further movement.

symptoms: nozzle grease calibration failure
auto calibration fails with greasy nozzle
residue on nozzle before calibration
fixes.title: Calibration fails with residue on the nozzle
fixes.likely_cause: Residue on the nozzle may interfere with the calibration contact. This seed explanation does not establish that every calibration failure has the same cause.
steps: Cancel calibration and let the nozzle cool fully.
Follow the official nozzle-cleaning procedure; if isopropyl alcohol is permitted for the affected surface, use it only with the printer off and cool, then let it evaporate.
Inspect the nozzle and run the official calibration sequence again after cleaning.
fixes.stop_if: The nozzle is damaged, a sensor fault appears, or calibration still fails. Keep the printer stock and send support the error and photos.

symptoms: vertical lines on walls at some speeds
vfa banding at 120 to 180 mm per second
fine vertical artifacts on straight walls
fixes.title: Vertical bands vary with wall speed
fixes.likely_cause: A community test associates these fine bands with particular wall speeds; actual results depend on the machine and filament.
steps: Run a VFA speed test with a profile that stays within the filament's usable flow range.
Compare banding across speeds before changing your saved profile.
Trial the linked report's 0.4 mm wall widths, Inner/Outer/Inner wall order and roughly 210 mm/s walls, then compare a small print.
fixes.stop_if: Extrusion becomes inconsistent or the test exceeds your measured flow capability. Reduce the demand and tune flow before repeating.

symptoms: prime tower keeps falling over
prime tower topples and causes layer shift
four color tower comes loose
fixes.title: Prime tower falls over
fixes.likely_cause: A loose or poorly supported tower can be struck during printing and disrupt the job. Check adhesion and layout before assuming a motion fault.
steps: Stop the job if the loose tower enters the toolhead path.
Check plate cleanliness and the tower's first-layer adhesion.
Review tower position, footprint and brim in the slicer. Try a modest layout change on a small job and inspect the toolhead path before repeating.
fixes.stop_if: A collision, layer shift or repeated adhesion failure returns after a controlled test. Save the project and ask support for help.

symptoms: runout sensor errors on one head
filament present but printer says runout
extruder gear jams on a specific head
fixes.title: One head reports filament runout incorrectly
fixes.likely_cause: The checklist flags a head-specific sensor or feed-path fault. A hotend problem can produce a similar loading failure.
steps: Record the affected head, error and filament before clearing anything.
Check the visible filament route and follow the official unload and inspection procedure.
Ask support whether the included spare hotend should be used to isolate the fault; perform any swap only under the official maintenance procedure.
fixes.stop_if: There is a jam that needs force, damage is visible, or the same head still fails. Stop and contact support while the machine is stock.

symptoms: psu fan whine at idle
right panel fan makes high pitched noise
power supply fan too loud
fixes.title: Idle fan whine near the PSU or right panel
fixes.likely_cause: The checklist records idle fan noise as something to baseline. Its location needs checking before choosing a cooling modification.
steps: Record a short clip and note whether the printer is idle or printing.
Check for an external object touching a panel or obstructing airflow without opening the machine.
During week one, send persistent noise to support. Review a documented cooling route only after stock checks are complete.
fixes.stop_if: There is grinding, a stalled fan, burning smell or loss of cooling. Turn the printer off safely and contact support.

symptoms: driver temps 85 to 92 degrees normal
orcaslicer shows hot stepper drivers
driver temperature around 90 celsius
fixes.title: Driver temperature readings look high
fixes.likely_cause: The owner checklist reports stock driver readings around 85–92°C and attributes reassurance to support. This is a baseline observation, not a universal safe limit or a main-processor reading.
steps: Record the exact sensor label, room conditions and workload alongside the reading.
Check that stock vents are unobstructed and compare with your own initial stock log.
Ask official support about the reading for your firmware and sensor if it is unfamiliar; keep processor and driver readings separate.
fixes.stop_if: There are thermal warnings, print failures, abnormal smells or stopped fans. Stop the job and consult support rather than relying on the seed temperature range.

symptoms: dryer feed lost rfid auto detection
filament from dryer not recognized
spool profile disappears when feeding from dry box
fixes.title: Dryer-fed filament is no longer identified
fixes.likely_cause: The built-in reader cannot scan a spool that has moved away into the dryer. Custom tags still need compatible firmware and proximity to the reader.
steps: Set the material and color manually for each affected feeder and verify the slicer assignments.
Check whether the physical spool or tag is within the reader's working range.
Optionally review OpenSpool NTAG215 setup on extended firmware; place a correctly written tag where the reader can actually scan it.
fixes.stop_if: The manual filament assignment is wrong or unreliable, or the tag is not detected after the documented checks. Resolve identification before starting a job.

source.creator: Paxx12; OpenSpool contributors
source.note: Reviewed project documentation for tag support and reader proximity.

provenance.note: Checklist warning retained. Tags are a conditional optional remedy, not automatic identification of distant dryer spools.

symptoms: cryogrip part stuck to plate
flat petg part welded to cryogrip
cannot remove print from cold grip plate
fixes.title: Part will not release from CryoGrip
fixes.likely_cause: Strong adhesion over a wide contact area can make removal difficult, particularly before the plate has cooled.
steps: Let the print and removable plate cool completely.
Follow BIQU's release instructions and use only gentle flexing within the plate's limits.
The checklist reports a short freezer chill as a release trick; check current plate guidance before trying it and keep condensation away from the printer.
fixes.stop_if: Release requires sharp tools, heavy force or surface damage. Pause and ask the plate vendor for guidance.

symptoms: pogo fan dropouts on one head
toolhead fan stops intermittently
one head fan loses power
fixes.title: One toolhead fan cuts out
fixes.likely_cause: An unreliable contact is one possibility in the checklist. A fan or wiring fault also needs ruling out through official support.
steps: Stop printing with the affected head and save the error or a video.
With the machine in the official maintenance state, inspect and photograph the pogo contacts.
Follow the official cleaning and reseating procedure, then ask support how to verify the fan before using that head again.
fixes.stop_if: The fan remains intermittent, any contact is damaged, or a temperature warning appears. Keep that head out of service and contact support.

symptoms: odor with top cover in external circulation mode
enclosure smells despite official filter
top cover exhaust instead of internal filtered mode
fixes.title: Odor persists with the official Top Cover
fixes.likely_cause: The brief suggests checking circulation mode. Odor alone cannot measure filtration effectiveness or establish whether the space is safe.
steps: Pause the job if fumes are escaping into an occupied space and follow the material's ventilation guidance.
Check the official cover guide for the mode required by your material; review internal filtered circulation rather than assuming external exhaust passes through the filter.
Check the filter installation and service interval before resuming, and ask support if the mode or airflow remains unclear.
fixes.stop_if: Odor persists, the fan or filter is faulty, or anyone is uncomfortable. Stop printing in that space and resolve ventilation and support guidance first.
